alanis morissette.directory_summary: Ottawa-born Alanis Morissette transformed from a teenage Canadian pop singer into one of the defining alternative-rock voices of the 1990s. Jagged Little Pill became a global blockbuster through songs including "You Oughta Know" and "Ironic," while its confessional writing and emotional directness reshaped expectations for women in mainstream rock. Her later catalogue extended that introspective approach well beyond the album that made her internationally famous.

maestro fresh wes.directory_summary: Toronto's Maestro Fresh Wes gave Canadian hip-hop its first major national commercial breakthrough. His 1989 album Symphony in Effect and "Let Your Backbone Slide" set certification and chart milestones for Canadian rap, while his inaugural JUNO rap win and later Canadian Music Hall of Fame induction underline how much institutional ground his career helped open for the generations that followed.
